## What this run established

1. **rk-k0m1 wiring works in production.** Preflight: "turn timeout: verifier/hard
   300000ms, prover/hard 300000ms" — the workers-level override reached both dispatchers.
   Zero exit-10s this run (opus needed nothing near the ceiling). The CODEX direction of
   the validation (the timeout that actually starved attempt 12) is DEFERRED to a
   codex-permitted session — this run cannot test it, by construction.
2. **The attempt-12 blocker is prover-specific, as predicted.** Opus decomposed the
   lemma into children 1.1–1.7 (+1.5.1) in ordinary turns — the step codex's 120s
   ceiling starved. Consistent with attempt-11 prior.
3. **Family fail-closed held under sustained load, live.** 15 accepts refused
   `cross-vendor-rejected same-family` on the load-bearing path; zero leaked into af.
   The honest single-vendor preflight (rk-id1) is now verified live end-to-end →
   rk-id1 CLOSED.
4. **GAP 11 remains dead.** parse-failed=0, bind-failed=0; the claude verifier's
   verdict envelopes parsed clean across 22 turns. The rk-xxp/rk-i19 bounded repair
   again never fired (nothing needed repair) — still live-unfired, residual stands.
5. **rk-rxq demonstrated live.** The abort fired at 1,533,460 ≥ 1,500,000 — a 33,460
   (2.2%) overshoot. The per-call reserve (8,000, output-only) is small against real
   attributed per-turn totals (94k–228k, cache-dominated), exactly the reserve-vs-
   reality gap the bead (as corrected by the M3 review) describes. Overshoot magnitude
   is modest because cache reads dominate; the blind spot would bite harder at low
   cache fractions.
6. **Driver economics under an unpromotable roster**: the run consumed the full cap
   re-dispatching nodes whose accepts could never apply (retry caps per node bound each
   node's turns at 2-3; breadth of the fresh decomposition kept legal dispatch
   available until budget exhaustion). Semantics worked as specified; whether the
   driver SHOULD keep spending on a roster the preflight proved unpromotable is a
   design question for the M4-boundary review — a preflight-hard-stop flag (refuse to
   run rather than warn) would have saved ~1.5M tokens here. Filed as a bead.
